subject: Cost vs latency options — batching, streaming & next steps
messages:
From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
To: Sophie Martin <sophie.martin@novamed.ai>, James Li <james.li@novamed.ai>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 22 Apr 2027 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Recap: Latency vs Cost options & next steps

Hi Sophie / James —

Great to meet earlier. Quick recap and suggested next steps so we can get the procurement path started:

Summary of what we heard on the call:
- Primary workload: document ingestion + clinical summarization for radiology reports. Typical request size ~1.2k tokens.
- Expected peak QPS: 30 requests/sec during ingest windows; average sustained ~6 r/s.
- Monthly token estimate: 200M–600M tokens depending on growth and retention choices (see attached estimate).
- Budget band indicated on call: $2k–$8k/month committed initially; long-term unit target mentioned: "$ per 1M tokens" target asked to be ~ $1,500/1M (we noted).

Key tradeoffs to validate:
1) Latency SLOs — you said 200ms P95 for clinical UI responses is ideal, but for batch summarization you can accept higher latency (~1–2s).
2) Cost vs performance — streaming + lower batch sizes gives better P95 but higher unit cost; aggressive batching or relaxed SLOs drops cost significantly.
3) Deployment mode — Hosted API is fastest to stand up; Dedicated pools give better unit economics at the volumes you sketched.

Requested items (next steps):
- Sophie/Jame s: please confirm the monthly token range you want us to scope (we used 200M/400M/600M in the attached). If procurement needs a formal quote, confirm the PO timeline and any SOC2 evidence items.
- Internal: Lauren/Vivek — can you validate two configurations (A/B) that meet the mix of 200ms UI SLO vs 1.2s batch SLO and provide high-level cost per 1M tokens for each?

I attached the token estimate spreadsheet we built during the call (novamed_token_estimate.xlsx).

Proposed follow-up: short procurement + tech sync on Friday 04/23 at 11am PT to lock the initial commitment. Is that OK?

Thanks,
Aditya Rao

From: Sophie Martin <sophie.martin@novamed.ai>

Cc: procurement@novamed.ai
Date: Thu, 22 Apr 2027 11:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Recap: Latency vs Cost options & next steps

Thanks Aditya — helpful summary. Couple clarifications from our side:

- The 200M–600M monthly range is right for Q3 ramp assumptions. For procurement we should expect to commit to a conservative baseline first (likely 250M/mo) then expand.
- The $1,500/1M tokens figure was an internal target — but we can be flexible if a clear path to lower unit costs exists by moving to dedicated capacity or by relaxing the UI SLO slightly.
- For the clinician UI, we really want the interactive feel to be ~300ms P95 rather than 200ms; 500ms starts to feel laggy for radiologists. For background batch jobs (nightly summarization) 1–3s is fine.

Procurement note: we need a line itemized quote (hosted vs dedicated) with committed volume discounts for 12 months. Also please include any ramp credits and the SLA language (availability + latency credits) so our legal can triage.

We can do the Friday 04/23 11am PT call — James and I will be there.

— Sophie
Sophie Martin
VP of Product, NovaMed
Sophie.Martin@novamed.ai

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sophie Martin <sophie.martin@novamed.ai>, James Li <james.li@novamed.ai>
Date: Thu, 22 Apr 2027 13:30:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Recap: Latency vs Cost options & next steps

Aditya / team — quick prescriptive options to bring on Friday's call. I focused on two realistic configs given NovaMed's mix of interactive UI + batch summarization.

Option A — Low-latency hybrid (UI-focused)\- Deployment: Hosted API + optional Dedicated pool for high-demand routes\- UI SLO: target 300ms P95 for UI requests (continuous streaming, small batch sizes, 0.5s max batching window)\- Batch SLO: 1.2s P95 for summarization if routed to dedicated batch workers\- Cost profile: approx $2,200 per 1M tokens (hosted, streaming heavy). With a 12-month committed Dedicated pool at ~250M/month baseline, blended unit drops to ~$1,350/1M after discounts and sustained usage credits.

Option B — Cost-optimized (batch-first)\- Deployment: Dedicated pool with autoscale and burst to hosted when spike occurs\- UI SLO: target 450–500ms P95 (more aggressive batching, prefix KV cache)\- Batch SLO: 1.5–3s P95\- Cost profile: approx $900–$1,100 per 1M tokens at 250M+/month commitment (depending on quantization profile and routing).

Notes and routing suggestions:
- Hybrid streaming for UI (Option A) reduces perceived latency but increases per-token cost.
- Set a small prefix cache for radiology templates to avoid re-tokenizing boilerplate and reduce unit tokens by ~8–12%.
- Recommend an initial 3-month canary: start Hosted with streaming for UI and a small Dedicated commit (250M/mo) for batch + burst; reassess after usage month 2 for re-banding.

Attachments I can share on Friday: a short pricing tier PDF and an example rollout plan (will attach redwood-pricing-tiers.pdf).

If Sophie/Jame s confirm the 250M baseline, I’ll draft a line-item quote + SLA snippet for procurement to review before Friday.

— Lauren Bishop
Director, Solutions & Pricing | Redwood Inference
lauren.bishop@redwood.ai

Subject: RE: Recap: Latency vs Cost options & next steps

Sophie / James — thanks for the quick replies and clarity on the 250M baseline. Short summary from our side ahead of Friday's procurement+tech sync:

1) Two priced options we'll bring to the call (line items + SLA):
   - "Hybrid low-latency" (Tier 1): streaming-first, 300ms UI P95 target, estimated blended $1,350/1M at 250M commit (includes ramp credits + 12-month term).
   - "Cost optimized" (Tier 2): dedicated-first, 450–500ms UI P95 target, estimated $1,000/1M at 250M commit (depends on quantization and routing policy).

2) Practical recommendation: Start with Hybrid low-latency for first 4–8 weeks to protect clinician experience, then switch heavier routes to Dedicated cost-optimized config as usage stabilizes. This minimizes early churn risk and gives procurement levers.

3) Prep items for Friday:
   - Sophie: confirm PO approver name & billing contact so we can prep a draft SOW/quote.
   - James: any security evidence pack items beyond SOC 2 Type II (we have KMS/HSM options and audit logs).
   - Procurement: we'll upload the formal quote and SLA snippet to the Drive link I shared earlier.

If that looks good I'll attach the redwood-pricing-tiers.pdf to the follow-up calendar invite and include a short one-page SOW. Meeting invite incoming for 04/23 11:00am PT.

Thanks — looking forward to Friday,
Aditya
